output.summary: The incident rise is best explained by a self-reinforcing loop. Interrupt load displaces reliability work, and overdue postmortem action items then recur as incidents (60% of Q3 SEV1-SEV2). The Storage exemption acts as a natural experiment: closing its backlog cut its incidents and pages while traffic stayed flat. Volume growth (+7%), the tool migration (SEV1-SEV2 are declared manually) and coverage gaps (fast acknowledgement, few overlapping incidents, a failed Networking pilot) do not explain the rise. The hiring freeze came after the rise began, though it worsens on-call frequency. Attrition causes are confounded between pay and on-call. The second primary slot would raise on-call frequency to about 1 in 3 and speed attrition. Ring-fencing engineers to clear recurring-failure action items is preferred. Incident-count targets are harmful given the 2023 gaming.
